newsitem.title: UK: UK Attorney General to decide on editor's error.
newsitem.headline: UK Attorney General to decide on editor's error.

text.p: The British government's top legal adviser was asked on Friday to rule whether the editor of the London Evening Standard newspaper should face contempt of court proceedings for publishing an article which caused the collapse of a court case.

Editor Max Hastings appeared in court to explain the article which resulted in the collapse of the trial of five Irish Republican Army prisoners and an armed robber charged in connection with an escape from top security Whitemoor Prison.
Judge Maurice Kay ended the trial on Thursday because of prejudicial publicity.
He ruled the six criminals, all held in a special secure unit at the jail in eastern England, should not be tried again on the charges.
Kay said Hasting's case would be referred to the Attorney-General to see if contempt of court proceedings should be brought.
"I shall refer the matter to the Attorney General with a report and he will have to decide what to do," Kay said.
Hastings immediately apologised for the article, which he said had appeared in the Standard as a result of human error.
"We are desperately sorry that a piece of carelessness in our office caused the abandonment of these proceedings.
"This is one of those mistakes that happen through human error," he told reporters after the hearing.
Legal restrictions meant that the men's criminal histories should not have been mentioned by the media during the trial.
The case ended after the defendants' legal team successfully argued that an article about Belmarsh prison, where the defendants are now being held, had prejudiced their trial.
